title: Looking back
hook: 331 days ago you breathed at the bottom of the hill

segments.voice: Yesterday: the funnel, and how to test a teaching. Your line: by their fruits.

Halfway up a real hill, there's a moment worth waiting for. You've been staring at your feet for an hour, at the next rock, the next root. It seems you've gone nowhere. Then you stop, turn around, and there it is: the parking lot is a speck, the town is a map, and the path you walked winds all the way up to where you're standing. You didn't feel yourself climbing. You just kept putting one foot down. That's where you are now. Six days from now, year one ends, so this last week is a lookout. Today, turn around.
screen: `STARING AT YOUR FEET.` → `THEN YOU TURN AROUND.` → `THE PATH, ALL THE WAY UP.`

segments.voice: Start at the bottom of the hill. The very first thing on this path was a breath. One breath, with the bell, and the discovery that in Latin, Greek and Hebrew, one word can mean both breath and spirit. Your line was wander, notice, come back. Then the camps. The stories: Marcus arguing with his blanket, Nasruddin looking for his key under the lamp, Zhuangzi and the butterfly, Hillel on one foot. The practices: breath, the evening review, the view from above, the digital sabbath, sunset. The text: Rumi's reed flute, with Marcus Aurelius beside him. And this last camp, the depths: visits to seven traditions as a guest, the Stoics up close, and the science of practice. Why look back at all? Kierkegaard, the walker from four days ago, wrote in his journal that life can only be understood looking backward, but has to be lived looking forward. In the middle of a day, you can't see the shape. From up here, you can. Just don't grade yourself. Some days you skipped, and some weeks the practice was one breath in a parked car. That counts. The habit study said one missed day doesn't reset anything. Look back the way you'd look at a friend's photos from a long trip: with curiosity, and a little wonder that they went so far. Notice what changed, even a little, and what didn't. Both are data. Both belong to the climb.
screen: `DAY ONE: ONE BREATH.` · `STORIES, PRACTICES, THE TEXT, THE DEPTHS.` · `UNDERSTOOD BACKWARD, LIVED FORWARD.` · `NOT A GRADE: A FRIEND'S PHOTOS.` · then, large: `HOW FAR.`

segments.voice: If you wrote anything down in the early days, a line, a list, a question, find it now or when you can and read it slowly; if you didn't, take day one's line: someone is in there, say hi. Then take one breath, the way you did at the bottom of the hill. Notice who is breathing now, and whether anything is different.
Looking back. Turning around on the path to see how far you've come, with curiosity, not a grade. Today's word.
Your line: how far. The top of year one is six days off. Day three hundred twenty-five, done.

howItsDone: Many traditions and many people mark the end of a season or year by looking back: rereading journals, reviewing the year's practice, and noticing what changed, without judgment.
